And they loaded upon them abundant provisions and water,
because a journey of three days was a desolate desert,
in which there is no water, nor any habitation.
And because those Bujah fought upon camels,
and their camels were startled by every sight and strange sound,
Anbasah commanded his forces, and they hung bells on the necks of their horses {OCR?}.
And they met the Bujah and broke them,
and they killed many of them.
And their king again submitted to the Arabs,
and began to give every year four hundred mithqāls of gold {OCR?}, as was customary.
At this time, Bukhtīshō‘ son of Gabriel, son of Bukhtīshō‘, son of George, son of Bukhtīshō‘ the Elamite, was renowned in medicine.
He served the Caliph al-Mutawakkil {OCR?},
and was greatly magnified by him,
to such an extent that he became his equal in dress and honor, and the abundance of estates {OCR?}, coursers, male slaves, and female slaves.
He was so beloved by the Caliph {OCR?},
that on one of the days, when he went in to the Caliph {OCR?},
and sat with him according to his custom upon the royal throne,
and the physician was wearing a Byzantine satin garment,
and the seam of its hem was slightly ripped,
the Caliph {OCR?} began conversing with him,
and he kept pulling at that seam until it reached the armpits {OCR?}.
And discourse was held between them concerning madmen and lunatics.
And the Caliph {OCR?} asked him:
"By what sign do you know that a madman needs to be bound in chains?" And Bukhtīshō‘,
because he had already noticed what the Caliph had done to his garment,
said to him:
"When the madman goes as far in ripping his physician's garment as reaching the armpits {OCR?},
then we know that he is in need of chains."
And al-Mutawakkil laughed until he fell upon his back,
and ordered for him robes of state and they clothed him.
Yet although he loved him so much,
at the end he envied him and plundered all his property,
after that famous banquet which that physician prepared for him,
in which he prepared five thousand tables:
on every table a roasted lamb,
and two hens,
and two young pigeons,
and three kinds of cooked foods,
and a dish of sweets,
and an abundance of semolina bread,
and cups and aromatics,
and snow.
